proofs.proof_tex:
Work on the certificate event specified in the statement, so that \(h_{G,e}\) is a nonzero element of the covariance coordinate ring of the model. Write
\[
N=|D|+|B|+n
\]
and identify the real support space for the free entries of \((\Lambda,\Omega)\) with \(\mathbb R^N\). The set
\[
\mathcal S_+=\{(\Lambda,\Omega)\in\mathbb R^N:\Omega\succ0\}
\]
is nonempty because it contains \((0,I_n)\), and it is Euclidean open because positive definiteness is open in the space of real symmetric matrices. It is Zariski dense in \(\mathbb C^N\): if a complex polynomial vanishes on \(\mathcal S_+\), it vanishes on a real open box contained in \(\mathcal S_+\); successive specialization in one coordinate and the fact that a nonzero univariate polynomial has only finitely many roots show inductively that every coefficient of that polynomial is zero.

Let \(\Phi_G(\Lambda,\Omega)=(I_n-\Lambda)^{-\mathsf T}\Omega(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}\). By the definition of the acyclic covariance homomorphism \(\phi_G\), the coordinates of \(\Phi_G\) are polynomials on the source space. By the established exceptional-set validity theorem, the restriction of \(h_{G,e}\) to the model image is nonzero. Equivalently, the source polynomial \(h_{G,e}\circ\Phi_G\) is nonzero. Zariski density of \(\mathcal S_+\) therefore supplies \((\Lambda_0,\Omega_0)\in\mathcal S_+\) for which
\[
h_{G,e}(\Phi_G(\Lambda_0,\Omega_0))\ne0.
\]
Putting \(\Sigma_0=\Phi_G(\Lambda_0,\Omega_0)\), the definition of \(\mathcal M_G\) gives \(\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M_G\), while the definition of \(\mathcal E_{G,e}\) gives \(\Sigma_0\notin\mathcal E_{G,e}\).

The model image is semialgebraic: it is the projection of the set described by the polynomial covariance equations, the linear support equalities for \(\Omega\), and the strict principal-minor inequalities expressing \(\Omega\succ0\). The exceptional complement and the finitely many sign conditions in the real-lifting formula are likewise semialgebraic. Apply the established semialgebraic-stratification lemma to a common refinement of these sets. Because the squarefreeness factor contained in \(h_{G,e}\) is nonzero at \(\Sigma_0\), all specialized roots are simple there. Along a connected stratum avoiding that factor, nonreal conjugate roots can enter or leave the real axis only through a multiple root; hence the number of real roots is constant. Refining by every sign condition in the real-lifting formula and invoking the established real-root-lifting theorem makes each root's extension label constant as well. The connected refined stratum through \(\Sigma_0\) is a cell \(\mathcal C_{G,e}\) of the kind required by the definition of a regular cell.

Choose a smooth chart \(u:U\to\mathbb R^s\) around \(\Sigma_0\), where \(s=\dim\mathcal C_{G,e}\). For sufficiently small \(\rho>0\), the inverse image
\[
\mathcal K_G=u^{-1}(\overline B(u(\Sigma_0),\rho))
\]
is contained in \(U\cap\mathcal C_{G,e}\). It is nonempty and compact and has nonempty relative interior in the cell; when \(s=0\), it is the singleton \(\{\Sigma_0\}\), which has the same properties in its relative topology.

It remains to prove nonemptiness of the retained set at every point of this compact class. Fix \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\subseteq\mathcal M_G\). By the definition of \(\mathcal M_G\), there are real supported \(\Lambda\) and \(\Omega\succ0\) such that \(\Sigma=\Phi_G(\Lambda,\Omega)\). Multiplication by \((I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(I_n-\Lambda\) gives
\[
\Omega=(I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-\Lambda).
\]
For every missing bidirected pair \(i\leftrightarrow j\notin B\), direct expansion of the \((i,j)\) entry yields
\[
\Omega_{ij}
=\sigma_{ij}
-\sum_{p\in\operatorname{pa}_D(i)}\lambda_{pi}\sigma_{pj}
-\sum_{q\in\operatorname{pa}_D(j)}\lambda_{qj}\sigma_{iq}
+\sum_{p,q}\lambda_{pi}\lambda_{qj}\sigma_{pq}
=F_{ij}(\Lambda,\Sigma).
\]
The noise-support restriction makes this quantity zero. Thus the real value \(\lambda_e\) has a complete real supported extension satisfying every residual equation, and the definition of \(\mathcal R_e\) gives \(\lambda_e\in\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\). Therefore \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\ne\varnothing\) throughout \(\mathcal K_G\), as claimed.

Put \(d=d_e(G)\). Since a field minimal polynomial has positive degree, \(d\ge1\), and write the monic polynomial supplied by the finite branch as
\[
p_e(\Sigma,t)=t^d+\sum_{a=0}^{d-1}c_a(\Sigma)t^a.
\]
Every \(c_a\) is represented by a rational covariance circuit. By the definition of the certificate exceptional set and the established exceptional-set validity theorem, each denominator, specialized-leading-coefficient factor, and squarefreeness factor used by these circuits is nonzero on \(\mathcal K_G\subset\mathcal C_{G,e}\). Each such factor is continuous on a neighborhood of \(\mathcal K_G\), so compactness gives a positive minimum for its absolute value. The numerator circuits are continuous as well and hence bounded on \(\mathcal K_G\). There is consequently a finite \(M\) such that
\[
\max_{0\le a<d}|c_a(\Sigma)|\le M
\qquad\text{for every }\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G.
\]

If \(z\) is a root and \(|z|>1+M\), then
\[
|z|^d
=\left|\sum_{a=0}^{d-1}c_a(\Sigma)z^a\right|
\le M\sum_{a=0}^{d-1}|z|^a
=M\frac{|z|^d-1}{|z|-1}
<|z|^d,
\]
a contradiction. Thus every specialized complex root lies in the fixed closed disk \(\{|z|\le1+M\}\). It follows that
\[
\mathscr Z=\{(\Sigma,z)\in\mathcal K_G\times\mathbb C:p_e(\Sigma,z)=0\}
\]
is closed in a compact set and therefore compact.

The nonvanishing squarefreeness certificate says that \(p_e(\Sigma,\cdot)\) and \(\partial_t p_e(\Sigma,\cdot)\) have no common root for every \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\). Hence \(\partial_t p_e\ne0\) on \(\mathscr Z\), and continuity and compactness imply
\[
\eta:=\min_{(\Sigma,z)\in\mathscr Z}|\partial_t p_e(\Sigma,z)|>0.
\]
Suppose no uniform root-separation constant existed. Then there would be \(\Sigma_\nu\in\mathcal K_G\) and distinct roots \(z_\nu,w_\nu\) of \(p_e(\Sigma_\nu,\cdot)\) with \(|z_\nu-w_\nu|\to0\). Compactness permits passage to a subsequence with
\[
(\Sigma_\nu,z_\nu,w_\nu)\longrightarrow(\Sigma_*,z_*,z_*).
\]
For every \(\nu\), the polynomial identity
\[
0=p_e(\Sigma_\nu,z_\nu)-p_e(\Sigma_\nu,w_\nu)
=(z_\nu-w_\nu)\int_0^1
\partial_t p_e\bigl(\Sigma_\nu,w_\nu+s(z_\nu-w_\nu)\bigr)\,ds
\]
and \(z_\nu\ne w_\nu\) imply, on taking limits, that \(\partial_t p_e(\Sigma_*,z_*)=0\). Continuity also gives \(p_e(\Sigma_*,z_*)=0\), contradicting the derivative bound above. Therefore some \(\gamma>0\) separates every two distinct complex roots uniformly on \(\mathcal K_G\). The retained real roots form a subset of these roots by exceptional-set validity and real-root lifting, so the same \(\gamma\) separates them.

Let \(q=n(n+1)/2\), use a fixed \(\operatorname{vech}\) ordering of the symmetric covariance entries, and define
\[
W_r=\operatorname{vech}\bigl(X^{(r)}X^{(r)\mathsf T}-\Sigma\bigr),
\qquad
\sqrt m\,\operatorname{vech}(S_m-\Sigma)=m^{-1/2}\sum_{r=1}^m W_r.
\]
The Gaussian sampling assumption gives \(\mathbb E_\Sigma W_r=0\). Differentiating the centered Gaussian moment-generating function \(\exp(t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma t/2)\) four times at zero gives
\[
\mathbb E_\Sigma[X_iX_jX_kX_l]
=\sigma_{ij}\sigma_{kl}+\sigma_{ik}\sigma_{jl}+\sigma_{il}\sigma_{jk}.
\]
Subtracting \(\mathbb E(X_iX_j)\mathbb E(X_kX_l)=\sigma_{ij}\sigma_{kl}\) therefore yields
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_\Sigma(W_{r,ij},W_{r,kl})
=\sigma_{ik}\sigma_{jl}+\sigma_{il}\sigma_{jk}
=(V_\Sigma)_{ij,kl}.
\]
Compactness of \(\mathcal K_G\) bounds the eigenvalues of \(\Sigma\) from above, so all Gaussian sixth moments, and hence \(\mathbb E_\Sigma\|W_r\|^3\), are bounded uniformly over \(\mathcal K_G\). For each fixed \(u\in\mathbb R^q\), Taylor's formula for \(e^{ix}\) consequently gives, uniformly in \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\),
\[
\mathbb E_\Sigma\exp\!\left(\frac{i u^{\mathsf T}W_r}{\sqrt m}\right)
=1-\frac{u^{\mathsf T}V_\Sigma u}{2m}+O(m^{-3/2}).
\]
Taking the \(m\)-th power shows that the characteristic function of the displayed normalized sum converges, uniformly in \(\Sigma\), to \(u\mapsto\exp(-u^{\mathsf T}V_\Sigma u/2)\). For completeness, this entails the asserted uniform weak convergence as follows. Uniformly bounded second moments make the laws of the normalized sums tight. From any sequence \((m_\nu,\Sigma_\nu)\) with \(m_\nu\to\infty\), compactness gives a subsequence on which \(\Sigma_\nu\to\Sigma_*\), and tightness gives a further weakly convergent subsequence. Its limiting characteristic function is \(\exp(-u^{\mathsf T}V_{\Sigma_*}u/2)\). A probability law is determined by its characteristic function: convolving two laws having the same characteristic function with \(N(0,\varepsilon I_q)\) gives equal smooth densities by Fourier inversion, and letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) gives equality of the original laws. Thus every subsequential limit is \(N(0,V_{\Sigma_*})\), which proves
\[
\sqrt m\,\operatorname{vech}(S_m-\Sigma)
\rightsquigarrow N(0,V_\Sigma)
\]
uniformly on \(\mathcal K_G\). Directly from the uniform second-moment bound,
\[
\|S_m-\Sigma\|=O_{\mathbb P}(m^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly on that compact class.

Put \(\widehat\Sigma_m=\pi_G(S_m)\) whenever \(S_m\) is in the projection tube. Since \(\pi_G(\Sigma)=\Sigma\) for \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\), smoothness of the projection and compactness give the uniform Taylor expansion
\[
\operatorname{vech}(\widehat\Sigma_m-\Sigma)
=D\pi_G(\Sigma)\operatorname{vech}(S_m-\Sigma)
+O(\|S_m-\Sigma\|^2).
\]
The coefficient circuits of \(p_e\) are smooth on a neighborhood of \(\mathcal K_G\), because all their denominator circuits are bounded away from zero there. The derived separation lemma gives \(\partial_t p_e(\Sigma,r_j(\Sigma))\ne0\) uniformly. Taylor expansion in the root coordinate, whose linear coefficient is bounded away from zero, gives a locally unique smooth solution branch by a contraction argument. Differentiating
\[
p_e(\Sigma,r_j(\Sigma))=0
\]
in the direction \(H\) gives the stated derivative
\[
Dr_j(\Sigma)[H]
=-\frac{D_\Sigma p_e(\Sigma,r_j(\Sigma))[H]}
{\partial_t p_e(\Sigma,r_j(\Sigma))}.
\]
Because distinct retained real roots are separated by \(\gamma\), increasing order gives a consistent labeling on the connected regular neighborhood. All first and second derivatives of these branches are bounded on a sufficiently small compact neighborhood of \(\mathcal K_G\). A second Taylor expansion and the preceding covariance central limit theorem now give
\[
\sqrt m\{r(\widehat\Sigma_m)-r(\Sigma)\}
\rightsquig
N\!\left(0,
Dr(\Sigma)D\pi_G(\Sigma)V_\Sigma
D\pi_G(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}Dr(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}
\right),
\]
with the middle juxtaposition interpreted as matrix multiplication; equivalently,
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_{\infty}
=Dr(\Sigma)D\pi_G(\Sigma)V_\Sigma D\pi_G(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}Dr(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}.
\]

We next construct the events in the statement. Every certificate factor is continuous and nonzero on \(\mathcal K_G\), so its absolute value has a positive minimum there. Compactness of \(\mathcal K_G\) inside the selected regular cell, the projection tube, and these strict certificate inequalities yields an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(\mathcal K_G\) on which the projection is defined, all certificates remain valid, and every extension label is unchanged. Uniform consistency of \(S_m\) and \(\widehat\Sigma_m\), uniform continuity of the roots, and the separation margin imply that the event
\[
\mathcal H_m=\left\{S_m\text{ lies in the projection tube},\quad
\widehat\Sigma_m\in U,\quad
\max_{1\le j\le J}|r_j(\widehat\Sigma_m)-r_j(\Sigma)|<\gamma/3\right\}
\]
satisfies
\[
\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}\Pr_\Sigma(\mathcal H_m)\longrightarrow1.
\]
On \(\mathcal H_m\), the exact characterization in the established real-root-lifting theorem, together with constancy of the extension labels, makes the estimator retain exactly \(r_1(\widehat\Sigma_m),\ldots,r_J(\widehat\Sigma_m)\). The \(\gamma/3\) inequalities make the correspondence with the population roots bijective. The regular-cell existence lemma gives \(J\ge1\), so the estimated set is nonempty on \(\mathcal H_m\). For two equally sized increasingly ordered real sets with this matching,
\[
d_H\bigl(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m},\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\bigr)
=\max_{1\le j\le J}|r_j(\widehat\Sigma_m)-r_j(\Sigma)|
=O_{\mathbb P}(m^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly. Moreover,
\[
\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}
\Pr_\Sigma(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\varnothing)
\le
\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}\Pr_\Sigma(\mathcal H_m^c)
\longrightarrow0.
\]

Finally, let \(s\) be the dimension of the selected smooth covariance stratum. If \(s=0\), each connected component is a point, the degenerate covariance ellipsoid contains that point with probability one once projection is defined, and simultaneous coverage is at least \(1-\alpha\). Suppose henceforth that \(s\ge1\). If \(a\ne0\) is a vector of symmetric-covariance coordinates and \(H_a\ne0\) is its associated symmetric matrix, then for \(X\sim N(0,\Sigma)\)
\[
\operatorname{Var}_\Sigma(X^{\mathsf T}H_aX)
=2\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma H_a\Sigma H_a)>0
\]
because \(\Sigma\succ0\). Thus \(V_\Sigma\) is positive definite on symmetric coordinates. The derivative of the nearest-point projection at a point of the stratum is the orthogonal projection onto its tangent space: it is the identity on tangent vectors because \(\pi_G\) fixes the stratum, and it annihilates normal vectors by the defining normal-fiber property of the tubular projection. Consequently
\[
W_\pi(\Sigma)
=D\pi_G(\Sigma)V_\Sigma D\pi_G(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}
\]
has constant rank \(s\), and its restriction to the tangent space is positive definite. Its smallest positive eigenvalue is bounded away from zero on \(\mathcal K_G\). The Moore--Penrose inverse \(W_\pi(\Sigma)^+\) is therefore continuous there. Substitution of \(\widehat\Sigma_m\) for \(\Sigma\) gives a uniformly consistent estimator \(\widehat W_{\pi,m}\), and the covariance central limit theorem together with the projection expansion gives
\[
m\,\operatorname{vech}(\widehat\Sigma_m-\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}
\widehat W_{\pi,m}^{+}
\operatorname{vech}(\widehat\Sigma_m-\Sigma)
\rightsquigarrow\chi_s^2
\]
uniformly. Let \(E_m\) be the set of covariance points in the regular tubular neighborhood satisfying the corresponding quadratic inequality at the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile. The preceding convergence and uniform consistency imply
\[
\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}\Pr_\Sigma(\Sigma\in E_m)
=1-\alpha+o(1).
\]
Define the branch neighborhoods, as in their construction, by
\[
\mathcal A_{m,j}=r_j(E_m),\qquad 1\le j\le J.
\]
Whenever \(\Sigma\in E_m\), every \(r_j(\Sigma)\) belongs to \(\mathcal A_{m,j}\) simultaneously. Therefore
\[
\liminf_{m\to\infty}\ \inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}
\Pr_\Sigma\!\left(r_j(\Sigma)\in\mathcal A_{m,j}
\text{ for all }1\le j\le J\right)
\ge1-\alpha.
\]
This proves simultaneous confidence validity without selecting a branch. The inequality is the sharp conclusion available for images of a covariance ellipsoid: absent local injectivity of the joint root map, image neighborhoods can be conservative.

Assume \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)=\{r_1(\Sigma)\}\) throughout \(\mathcal K_G\). This singleton assumption already gives constant cardinality one. On the events \(\mathcal H_m\) supplied by the regular finite-set inference theorem, the estimated retained set is bijectively matched to the population retained set. It therefore has exactly one element, denoted \(\widehat r_m\), and
\[
\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}
\Pr_\Sigma\bigl(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\{\widehat r_m\}\bigr)
\longrightarrow1.
\]
Define \(\widehat r_m=0\) on the complementary event; this modification occurs with uniformly vanishing probability and therefore does not affect consistency or weak convergence.
On the same events the singleton Hausdorff distance is ordinary absolute error, so
\[
|\widehat r_m-r_1(\Sigma)|
=d_H\bigl(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m},\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\bigr)
=O_{\mathbb P}(m^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly over \(\mathcal K_G\). This proves consistency. Taking the first coordinate in the joint limit of the regular finite-set inference theorem gives
\[
\sqrt m\{\widehat r_m-r_1(\Sigma)\}
\rightsquigarrow N(0,W_{11}(\Sigma)),
\]
where
\[
W(\Sigma)=Dr(\Sigma)D\pi_G(\Sigma)V_\Sigma
D\pi_G(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}Dr(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Thus \(W_{11}(\Sigma)\) is precisely the corresponding diagonal entry asserted in the proposition. If it is zero, the conclusion is the degenerate centered normal law, which requires no additional nondegeneracy assumption.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\). There are events \(\mathcal H_m\) with \(\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}(\mathcal H_m)\to1\) such that, on \(\mathcal H_m\), \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}\) is nonempty and is bijectively matched to \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\). With the empty-set convention in \(d_H\), uniformly over \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\), \(d_H(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m},\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma))=O_{\mathbb P}(m^{-1/2})\) and \(\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\varnothing)\to0\). Under local branch labels,
\[
\sqrt m\{r(\pi_G(S_m))-r(\Sigma)\}\rightsquigarrow N\!\left(0,Dr(\Sigma)D\pi_G(\Sigma)V_\Sigma D\pi_G(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}Dr(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}\right).
\]
The simultaneous neighborhoods \(\mathcal A_m\) cover every retained branch with asymptotic probability at least \(1-\alpha\), uniformly on \(\mathcal K_G\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Mapping a nominal covariance ellipsoid through the branch maps guarantees simultaneous coverage at least at the nominal level. Without local injectivity of the joint retained-root map, the image can cover all true branches even when the covariance is outside the ellipsoid, so equality of the resulting coverage probability is not justified.

proposed.statement: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\) and the certificate event on which \(h_{G,e}\) is nonzero. The real supported source set \(\{(\Lambda,\Omega):\Lambda\in\mathbb R^D,\ \Omega\succ0,\ \Omega_{ij}=0\text{ if }i\leftrightarrow j\notin B\}\) is Euclidean open in its support space and Zariski dense in the complex source space. Since \(\mathcal E_{G,e}\) is proper on the model image, there is a real supported source point \((\Lambda_0,\Omega_0)\) whose covariance \(\Sigma_0\) lies in \(\mathcal M_G\setminus\mathcal E_{G,e}\). A smooth semialgebraic stratification refined by the real-lifting sign conditions contains \(\Sigma_0\) in a connected cell \(\mathcal C_{G,e}\) on which real-extension status is constant, and a sufficiently small closed chart ball gives a nonempty compact \(\mathcal K_G\subset\mathcal C_{G,e}\) with nonempty relative interior. For every \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\), \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\ne\varnothing\), because membership in \(\mathcal M_G\) supplies at least one complete real supported \(\Lambda\).
proposed.justification: The regular statistical domain must be shown nonvacuous and its real identified set must be nonempty rather than imposed by assumption.
proposed.gap: Standard stratification arguments isolate smooth cells, but the stated lemma ties such a cell to the certified SEM exceptional locus and to rootwise real extension.
proposed.consumer: The inference theorem obtains a genuine compact operating region and a nonempty target set on every data-generating covariance in that region.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses closure of semialgebraic sets under projection to establish that the covariance-model image and the real-lifting refinement are semialgebraic. The frozen effective quantifier-elimination lemma supplies exactly that premise and must be a direct dependency.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a source-prime-preserving finite-branch elimination routine for every recorded pole and zero-over-zero stratum, and use it to return the true coordinate minimal polynomial and every required nonzero exceptional-set circuit within the asserted fixed-parameter time and certificate bound.
open_obligations.obstruction: The established quadratic-core lemma is extensional: it bounds variables and degrees and preserves the queried projection degree, but it does not provide a bounded prime-component presentation or an incidence-lifting identity selecting the component induced by the integral source incidence algebra. Elimination on the union can introduce queried values from extraneous components, while deleting divisor strata can lose genuine branches. The missing selection and lifting data are also needed for the slice-coverage, pole, projective-leading-form, specialized-leading-coefficient, squarefreeness, and real-lifting circuits. Assuming such data would assume the algorithmic crux of the theorem.
open_obligations.attempted: I carried the prior Jacobian-rank route through a complete algebraicity decision and transcendental dominance certificate, and reduced the algebraic branch to bounded multiplication-matrix linear algebra after a correct source-prime slice is supplied. I also examined elimination of all divisor strata together and selective saturation by recorded denominators; the former admits extraneous components and the latter deletes legitimate zero-over-zero components, so neither certifies the required minimal polynomial.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The transcendental output tag and the finite-branch reduction can be established, but the certified finite-branch component selection cannot be obtained from the frozen premises. Write the algebraically independent source coordinates as
\[
\theta=(\lambda_D,\omega_B,\omega_{\mathrm{diag}})
=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_N)
\]
and enumerate the distinct covariance generators of \(K_G\) as
\(f_a=\phi_G(\sigma_{i_a j_a})\), \(1\le a\le s\). Over
\(L=\mathbb C(\theta)\), define
\[
J_0=\left(\frac{\partial f_a}{\partial\theta_b}\right)_{a,b},
\qquad
J_1=
\begin{pmatrix}
J_0\\
\left(\dfrac{\partial\lambda_e}{\partial\theta_b}\right)_b
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For arbitrary rational functions \(g_1,\ldots,g_u\in L\),
\[
\operatorname{rank}_L
\left(\frac{\partial g_a}{\partial\theta_b}\right)_{a,b}
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C(g_1,\ldots,g_u).
\]
Indeed, choose a transcendence basis \(v_1,\ldots,v_r\) of
\(\mathbb C(g_1,\ldots,g_u)/\mathbb C\). Characteristic zero makes the algebraic extensions separable. Differentiating the separable algebraic equations shows that the \(dg_a\)'s and the \(dv_i\)'s span the same \(L\)-subspace of \(\Omega^1_{L/\mathbb C}\). Extending the \(v_i\)'s to a transcendence basis of \(L/\mathbb C\) makes \(dv_1,\ldots,dv_r\) linearly independent, proving the equality. Applying it to the covariance generators and then to those generators together with \(\lambda_e\) gives
\[
\operatorname{rank}_LJ_1-\operatorname{rank}_LJ_0
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{K_G}K_G(\lambda_e)
=
\begin{cases}
0,&\lambda_e\text{ is algebraic over }K_G,\\
1,&\lambda_e\text{ is transcendental over }K_G.
\end{cases}
\]
This is an algebraicity test in the source function field, not an inference from local Jacobian rank at a numerical specialization.

Acyclicity gives \(\Lambda^n=0\) after topological ordering and therefore
\[
(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\Lambda^j.
\]
All entries of \(J_0\) and \(J_1\) consequently have source-polynomial circuits of size polynomial in \(n\). After row and column permutations, a rank-\(r\) transcript has block form
\[
J=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det A\ne0,
\qquad D-CA^{-1}B=0,
\]
where \(A\) is \(r\times r\). Multiplication by \(\det A\) turns the last display into polynomial-circuit identities. A nonzero exact evaluation proves \(\det A\not\equiv0\); independently sampled source evaluations test the remaining zero identities. The Schwartz--Zippel bound, with a union bound over the polynomially many identities and a sampling set chosen as a function of \(\delta\), limits the total symbolic error to \(\delta\) with polynomial arithmetic work and \(\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\) random-bit and transcript overhead.

If the ranks differ, the map
\[
K_G[t]\longrightarrow A_K,
\qquad t\longmapsto\lambda_e,
\]
is injective. Indeed, a nonzero kernel element would be an algebraic equation for \(\lambda_e\) over \(K_G\), contrary to the rank calculation. Since the established incidence-localization theorem makes \(A_K\) integral with fraction field \(L\), the induced morphism
\[
\operatorname{Spec}(A_K)\longrightarrow\mathbb A^1_{K_G}
\]
is dominant; its irreducible source has positive dimension. The two rank transcripts thus instantiate \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) and complete the transcendental tag within the asserted fixed-parameter bound.

On the algebraic branch, the established quadratic-core lemma reduces the calculation to at most \(r\le2k\) exposed variables and equations of degree at most two with rational-circuit coefficients in \(K_G\). If a source-prime-preserving zero-dimensional slice of the appropriate recorded divisor stratum is given, its quotient degree is at most \(2^r\). Linear algebra on the multiplication operator for \(\lambda_e\), followed by its first monic linear dependence and squarefree factor selection, computes the coordinate eliminant. The established orientation upper bound improves the degree of the true irreducible coordinate factor to at most \(2^{k+1}\). These operations use \(n^{O(k+1)}\) arithmetic once the correct stratum and slice have been certified.

The unresolved step is prior to that linear algebra. The quadratic-core lemma is extensional: it asserts projection-degree preservation after recording pole and zero-over-zero cases, but it gives neither a bounded-size prime-component presentation for each such case nor a lifting identity selecting the component induced by the integral source incidence algebra. A rational-univariate representation of the union can add coordinate values from extraneous components, whereas deleting divisor components can remove genuine finite branches. The same absent presentation is needed to produce bounded nonzero circuits for slice coverage, incidence lifting, poles, projective leading forms, specialized leading coefficients, squarefreeness, and real lifting. Thus the transcendental tag and the conditional multiplication-matrix stage are proved, while the exact finite tag and its certificate-size guarantee remain open.
